newsitem.title: USA: Charleston, S.C., tentatively OKs $85 mln of bonds.
newsitem.headline: Charleston, S.C., tentatively OKs $85 mln of bonds.

text.p: South Carolina's Charleston County Council gave preliminary approval for an $85 million bond issue to renovate a hospital building for doctors affiliated with the Medical University of South Carolina.
In a change of course, the council approved the revenue bond issue 5-3 Tuesday night.

Proceeds would finance renovation of the Bon Secours-St Francis Xavier Hospital building for use by University Medical Associates. The nonprofit group is made up of doctors who teach and treat patients at the the university.
The council rejected the bond issue two months ago because of concerns by other private physicians about a university plan to lease its hospitals to a for-profit company.
The bond issue was reconsidered after the county attorney advised that the council had approved similar arrangements for other hospitals in the past.
Additionally, county spokeswoman Jamie Thosams said the county would not be liable if the doctors' group defaults on the bonds.
A final vote is scheduled following a public hearing on Dec 3. The bond issue would then have to be approved by the South Carolina Budget and Control Board.
